caption:
Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund.
Elon Musk replied on X that the shares should go directly to the public, then added: "This is what I will be doing."
He has not said which shares, to whom, or when.

Should AI companies hand their stock straight to people?

Source: Benzinga, The Hans India, Anthropic

slides.headline: Elon Musk tells Anthropic to give its shares *directly to the public*, says he'll do it too

slides.heading: Musk's *two-post* reply
paras: Anthropic announced Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund. Musk answered on X: "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public."
In a follow-up post he added: "This is what I will be doing." He gave no details on which shares, who gets them or when.

slides.heading: What Anthropic *actually* pledged
paras: The plan still needs stockholder approval. The board can add 2% more shares for every 50% rise in Anthropic's value above a baseline it has not disclosed.
The fund could back nonprofits, pay specific groups of people directly and address AI's impact on jobs. None of its stock can go to lobbying or political giving.

slides.heading: A fund, not a *handout*
paras: The fund is set up as a wholly owned LLC, not a 501(c)(3) charity. Anthropic says that gives it more flexibility in how the money is used.
Musk questioned whether a middleman fund is the best route. Anthropic says details on governance and structure will come in the coming months.

slides.heading: Not his *first shot* at Anthropic
paras: In February, Musk called Anthropic "misanthropic and evil" and told the company to "Fix it." He runs xAI, a direct rival.

paras.t: Anthropic says about 20% of its shares are now set aside for the public good as it prepares for a possible IPO.

slides.hook: Musk says he will hand shares straight to the public. Follow to see if he actually does it.
